A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RINS research despite the changed title and organization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained content against substantive additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, downstream reasoning evaluations, vision experiments, and multilingual SigLIP results, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of linear adapters and KV-cache sharing, alongside revised downstream reasoning results.

M1.justification: The core ArB recursion and stochastic skipping remain unchanged. However, v3 Section 6 introduces recursion-count-specific linear adapters before the output projection head and a variant that reuses the first A pass's cached keys and values. These add substantive model and inference components.

E1.justification: Table 1 and Appendix C remove WinoGrande and add HellaSwag sentence completion and CommonsenseQA, while retaining OpenBookQA, BoolQ, PIQA, and SIQA. Language pretraining, vision, multilingual, and multimodal coverage otherwise remain unchanged; the vision experiments are relocated, not removed.

E2.justification: The baseline, RAO, long-sequence comparisons, and architecture sweep retain their comparator membership. v3 newly associates Geiping et al.'s latent recurrent thinking with ABrC, but the ABBC pattern already appears in v1's unchanged sweep; this does not establish an additional evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix C changes BoolQ from unprompted concatenation to an explicit passage-and-question template. New Figure 6 evaluates 600M-parameter adapter-equipped models with skip probabilities 0.5 and 0.8 and introduces cache-sharing controls. The principal existing training configurations and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v3 Section 6 and Figure 6 add investigations of whether adapters avoid the penalty from disabling recursion at inference and whether RINS retains benefits when recursive passes share a KV cache. These substantially extend the practical analysis beyond v1's recursion-count, stochastic-skipping, and scaling-law studies, which remain present.

E5.justification: v3 Table 1 adds ± uncertainty values where v1 reported point accuracies. Their meaning, calculation, and run counts are not specified, so additional repeated runs cannot be inferred. The SigLIP Wilcoxon test and reported p = 0.003 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises retained-task scores and adds and removes benchmark results. For example, OpenBookQA changes from RAO/RINS accuracies of 38.3/38.9% to 40.0 ± 0.6/39.0 ± 0.3%, reversing their reported ranking. Figure 6 adds favorable adapter and cache-sharing findings. BoolQ scores use a changed prompt and are not same-setting gains; retained vision and multimodal table values match.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1 and 2.2, the signature/degree framework, binomial recursion sampling, and power-law formulation remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies new theoretical proofs, and v3's added components are described procedurally rather than through new formal derivations.

C1.justification: v1 claims that stochastic RINS permits non-recursive inference with minimal degradation. v3 strengthens this into an adapter-assisted 'no-regret' pretraining claim: improved language modeling even without recursive inference, with training compute, parameters, and inference cost described as matched. It also adds retained benefits under KV-cache sharing as an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets adapters as resolving the earlier flexibility-versus-performance tradeoff and conjectures that improved inductive bias explains gains without recursive inference. It newly acknowledges that KV-cache sharing diminishes RINS's advantage. The language self-similarity hypothesis and lack of benefit in pure vision remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 documents adapter placement and selection, their less-than-1% parameter overhead, first-pass KV reuse, and the new BoolQ prompt. Its checklist explicitly discloses that experimental code and models are not released. Existing training configurations and hardware information are retained rather than newly supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds Geiping et al. (2025) and positions RINS against latent recurrent thinking, emphasizing compute-matched and multimodal distinctions. It also adds HellaSwag and CommonsenseQA references while removing WinoGrande and several background citations. The broader related-work account remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, substantially revises the abstract and contribution narrative, reorganizes the modality discussion, and moves vision and pseudocode material into dedicated appendices. It repairs the configuration-section organization, removes accidental drafting text from Appendix C, and adds a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to one, with extensively rearranged tables and figures. Existing plots are merged or split between the main text and appendices, retrieval tables are redistributed, and Figure 6 is new. v3 Table 3 also introduces a labeling defect: its skip-probability headers are shifted one column left.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful practical evidence addressing v1's penalty when recursion is disabled and its untested KV-cache memory tradeoff (Section 6, Figure 6). Appendix organization and evaluation documentation also improve. These gains are qualified by the narrow new evaluations, undefined Table 1 error bars, and newly misaligned Table 3 headers, supporting a limited net improvement.
